subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should exact npm scope identity, including dots and underscores, be the permanent ClawHub publisher ownership boundary?
rationale: The implementation is shipped, but collaborator authorship requires human handling and the identity grammar governs authorization across publishing, routing, repair, and transfer flows.

options.title: Accept exact scopes
options.body: Keep npm-compatible publisher handles and document their grammar plus exact scope equality in the ownership specification.

options.title: Adopt verified aliases
options.body: Design a first-class alias mapping with equivalent authorization guarantees across publishing, installation, repair, transfer, and UI flows.

options.title: Require package renames
options.body: Return to slug-safe handles and require affected packages to adopt new npm scopes.

recommendation.title: Accept exact scopes
recommendation.body: Keep npm-compatible publisher handles and document their grammar plus exact scope equality in the ownership specification.

likelyOwner.reason: The specification, implementation, release, and recent area history make this person the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
